# Entire Graph

Coding agents lose time before the edit, while they are still looking for the
right code. Entire Graph is a plugin for the Entire CLI that gives an agent a
precomputed map of one Git repository: ranked code search plus definitions,
callers, types, routes, and change impact, each with `file:line` locations. The
built-in analyzer parses the repository locally with tree-sitter and makes no
network requests, model calls, or API-key lookups. Installing the plugin is the
networked step.

Setup happens once per repository. After that, the interface is your coding
agent: you ask a code question in plain language, the agent runs graph queries,
reads the code the graph points at, and answers with citations. A captured
example is shown below.

## Benchmarks

(1,540 questions, shared reader and judge, a 200-item retrieval budget requested for

[v0.4.0](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/releases/tag/v0.4.0) (tagged four days later,

## Install

Entire Graph requires Entire CLI 0.10.0 or later and Git 2.36 or later on
`PATH`. Git 2.36 added the single-session object protocol Entire Graph uses to
inspect an object's type before reading its contents. The commands below are
the official ones from the [Entire CLI installation
guide](https://docs.entire.io/installation), which also covers Windows and
other channels.

On macOS:

```sh
brew tap entireio/tap
brew trust entireio/tap
brew install --cask entire
```

On Linux:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
```

Then **install the plugin** from the plugin index and confirm its version:

```sh
entire plugin install graph
entire graph version
```

`entire graph version` printing a release tag confirms that a versioned build
is active.
The local install helper reports the source checkout's Git description; a raw
unversioned build prints `dev` (see [operations](docs/operations.md)).

## Activate it for your agent

Activation is per repository:

```sh
entire graph init-agents --repo .
```

The command creates or updates these files:

- `.entire/graph-agent.md`: the agent operating guide. Generated in full and
  regenerated in full on each successful rerun; manual edits there do not
  survive.
- `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`: created if absent; otherwise one managed block
  between `<!-- entire-graph:begin -->` and `<!-- entire-graph:end -->` markers
  is added or replaced. Text outside the markers is preserved.

Review the three files, then commit them together when the instructions should
apply to your team.

built with React + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind + `@react-three/fiber`.

## What it is

Same data, same six-tier model, same radial blast-radius 3D scene as the
Go-rendered dashboard — reimplemented as real components instead of one
generated HTML blob, so it's actually maintainable as a UI:

- `src/types.ts` — TypeScript types mirroring `verdict.go`'s `Verdict` struct
  field-for-field (kept in sync by hand, no generator).

  edges exist only for `expected_blast_radius`; every other tier is an
  unconnected, tier-colored node placed in its own radial zone.
- `src/components/graph/` — the Three.js scene as `@react-three/fiber`
  components (`Nodes`, `Edges`, `HopRings`, `BlastRadiusScene`), using drei's
  `OrbitControls`/`Stars`/`Sparkles` and `@react-three/postprocessing`'s
  `Bloom` instead of hand-rolled Three.js — the same visual result as the
  Go-rendered scene, written as idiomatic React instead of imperative
  `useEffect` DOM manipulation.
- `src/components/SummaryTab.tsx`, `TierCard.tsx`, `TierList.tsx` — the
  tier-grouped summary view.
- `src/hooks/useReveal.ts` — reveal-on-scroll, **with a fix for a real bug**
  found in the Go-rendered version's equivalent: there, elements started
  `opacity:0` and depended entirely on an `IntersectionObserver` callback to
  ever appear, and in one real browser session that callback never fired —
  the content stayed permanently invisible. This hook adds a mount-time
  fallback timer so a browser quirk degrades to "no fade-in animation"
  instead of "the content never appeared."

**The big idea:** someone asked an AI to make a code change. Fidelity checks — did it do what was asked, and did it also touch stuff nobody asked for?

**Sidebar (left)**
- The 6 links are the buckets every changed thing falls into. Numbers = how many landed in each.
- Bottom pill (`REVIEW_REQUIRED`) = the overall call. Red = a human needs to look.
- "← Back to site" = go to the landing page.

**Overview**
- 4 tiles = count per bucket, at a glance.
- "Tier mix" bars = same counts, as bar lengths.
- "Checkpoint" = which two code snapshots were compared, and when.

**Confirmed**
- "Confirmed" table = things the prompt asked for that actually got changed. Good.
- "Expected Blast Radius" table = other code that got dragged in because it connects to a confirmed change. The "hops" number = how many steps away it is.

**Advisory**
- Changes that *might* match the ask, but the evidence is weak/guessed. Look, but don't panic.

**Unverifiable**
- Changes the tool couldn't see clearly. It tells you which file or test to check by hand.

**Scope Creep**
- "Undeclared Scope Creep" = changed, but nobody asked for it. The risky part.
- "Declared Unimplemented" = asked for, but never done.

**Graph View**
- The same buckets as a 3D map. Center = confirmed changes. Distance from center inside the green core = real number of steps away. Outer rings = the uncertain/unseen/unasked stuff. Click a dot for details.

content.text:
## Short version

- **The graph engine** (`search`, `impact`, `diff`, `snapshot`) — **yes, works on PyCharm's repo today.** PyCharm ships inside `JetBrains/intellij-community`, which is Java + Kotlin, and both are **fully semantic** in the tool (calls, inheritance, type edges — not just "list of names"). A giant monorepo is a fair "complex repo" flex.

- **`verify-intent` + the Fidelity dashboard** — **not directly.** It doesn't take "any two commits + a prompt". Its only input is an **Entire checkpoint ID**, and a checkpoint is an *AI-agent session transcript* stitched onto a commit by Entire's git hooks. PyCharm's public history has zero of those, and there's no `--prompt` flag to fake one.

## What's actually possible

**Option A — graph engine on intellij-community (works now, low effort)**
Clone it, point the graph at the `python/` subtree (the PyCharm-specific code — the full monorepo is ~4 GB and millions of LOC, so scope it), then run `entire graph impact --symbol … ` / `diff --base … --head …` / `snapshot`. Shows it scaling to JetBrains-size Java/Kotlin.

**Option B — a real verdict on PyCharm's code (earns the bonus + demos the frontend)**
1. Shallow-clone intellij-community locally.
2. Run a change *through an Entire-wired agent* in that clone — e.g. "add method X to class Y" — which creates a checkpoint.
3. `entire graph verify-intent <checkpoint-id> --out fidelity-out/` → `verdict.json`.
4. Open it in the dashboard.
   → "we pointed our tool at a change in PyCharm's codebase and it reconciled intent-vs-diff on Java at that scale."

Option B is the honest product demo; A is the warm-up. Want me to set up A (clone + a few graph queries on the `python/` subtree) so you have something concrete to show?

# entire-graph on PyCharm's source (JetBrains/intellij-community)

**Repo under test:** `JetBrains/intellij-community` — the mono-repo PyCharm Community ships from.
Scoped to the `python/` subtree (the PyCharm Python plugin) via a sparse checkout.

**Scale of the slice:** 228 MB working tree, ~19k source files —
**2,520 Java · 2,346 Kotlin · 14,060 Python**.
Java, Kotlin and Scala are all *semantic* languages in the tool (real call / inheritance /
type edges), not name-only.

**Tool build:** local `entire-graph` binary (`8f3eef6`), no network, tree-sitter parsers.

---

## What ran

| Command | Result | Cold time |
|---|---|---|
| `search "python code completion contributor"` | Found `PyKeywordCompletionContributor.java` **and** a Kotlin sibling, call-graph signal resolved | ~2 min (cold index) |
| `def --symbol PyKeywordCompletionContributor` | Full class: ~39 fields, method surface, 5 nested classes, **supertypes `CompletionContributor [extends]`, `DumbAware [implements]`** | ~95 s |
| `neighbors --symbol putKeyword --relation CALLS --direction in` | Real callers with exact call sites; `Query: 24 ms` once indexed | ~80 s (index), 24 ms query |
| `diff --base de251fd3a --head 35530ce75` (real commit `PY-91150`) | Cross-language entity diff, see below | **2.7 s** (warm cache) |

Parse completeness on the slice: **0 of 2,520 Java files failed to parse.** A handful of
Kotlin files (`PyTypeCheckerInspection.kt`, `PyCallExpressionHelper.kt`) hit tree-sitter
grammar limits on newer syntax — surfaced as explicit `E_PARSE_ERROR` warnings, not silent
drops. The ~4,100 Python "diagnostics" are mostly intentionally-malformed test fixtures
(this repo *is* the Python parser's test corpus).

---

## Semantic diff of a real PyCharm commit

`35530ce75` — **"PY-91150 Do not bind a nested class to `self`"** (base = its parent `de251fd3a`):

**`python/python-psi-impl/.../PyReferenceExpressionImpl.java`** (Java, `M`)
- `class PyReferenceExpressionImpl` — body_changed — **dependents_count: 20**
- `method PyReferenceExpressionImpl.getTypeOfClassMember` — body_changed — dependents_count: 2

**`python/testSrc/.../PyDataclassTypeTest.kt`** (Kotlin, `M`)
- `class PyDataclassTypeTest` — body_changed
- **added** `class NestedDataclassThroughInstance` — `@Nested inner class …`
- **added** `fun \`nested dataclass called through self\`()` — `@Test @TestFor(issues = ["PY-91150"])`
- **added** `fun \`nested dataclass passed as an argument through instance\`()` — `@Test @TestFor(issues = ["PY-91150"])`

One command, Java implementation + Kotlin test, entity-level, each with a real
dependent count (blast radius).

---

## Caveats

- **Cold first query is slow** (~1–2 min to build the graph over 19k files); everything after
  is seconds while the cache is warm. `entire-graph index --head` up front fixes this.
- **`diff` needs a normal clone.** A `--filter=blob:none` partial + sparse + shallow clone
  makes the tool refuse ("unsafe or unreadable repository metadata"). Fix: drop the blob
  filter and `git fetch --depth=40` (brought the repo to ~390 MB, no full clone needed).
- **`verify-intent` / the Fidelity dashboard was NOT run** — it requires an Entire *checkpoint*
  (an agent-session transcript), which no upstream GitHub repo has. That's Option B (make a
  change here through an Entire-wired agent, then verify its intent).

## Reproduce

```sh
git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/JetBrains/intellij-community.git
cd intellij-community && git sparse-checkout set python
git config --unset remote.origin.partialclonefilter && git fetch --depth 40 origin   # only needed for `diff`
```
